Services for clients

What you can hire me to write

Three kinds of work, all built the same way: we agree the outline and the voice first, then I draft to milestones so you always know where the project stands.

For authors & clients with a book to tell

Ghostwriting

Full-length manuscripts written in your voice, from your story, your characters, and your material. You remain the author of the ideas; I do the writing work of turning them into a finished draft.

The process is outline-first. We lock the structure and voice before drafting begins, then work to milestone deadlines with strict version control — so there is never confusion about which draft is current or what changed.

Ask about ghostwriting

What this includes

  • Outline first — structure agreed before drafting
  • Written in your voice — from your story & characters
  • Milestone deadlines — draft delivered in stages
  • Strict version control — one clear current draft
  • Full-length manuscripts — fiction, including fantasy & horror

Dialogue samples · Two-Week Dialogue Intensive

Taking out the Trash

by Andrew McCaslin · Coursework sample

A short piece from the Two-Week Dialogue Intensive, presented verbatim. The whole story is carried by the conversation: a husband hiding something in the basement, and his wife’s voice completely distinct from his.

A 335-word piece carried entirely by conversation — a husband keeping his wife away from whatever is in the basement, the subtext never stated outright.

Coursework sample — read in full below

The TV's light filled the otherwise dark room, a dancing kaleidoscope of color shifting with the screen's movement. The volume was low enough for him to hear.

The familiar screech of the basement door opening hit him like a cannon. No! His breath hitched, dread seizing him as he shot from his chair, heart hammering, and bolted toward the sound. He rounded the corner, skidding on the carpet, his feet scrambling for purchase as he snatched the bag of garbage his wife was holding.

“Hey,” he said, trying to control his breathing and heart rate. “I got this.”

“What are you doing?” she said with a chuckle. “You're being weird. Get off.” She shook the bag as if to dislodge him, her other hand still holding her phone on speaker.

“Why are you using the basement? Just use the front door,” he said, his grip firm on the bag.

“It's closer to the can, what's your problem?” Her humor drained, annoyance creeping into her tone.

“It's dark outside. I won't allow you to go out.” Come on, take the bait.

“Ooohhh,” the voice on speakerphone chimed with scandalized excitement.

“Girl,” she said, pulling the phone closer. “I'mma have to let you go. This boy's acting a fool.” Not waiting for a response, she ended the call, her eyes narrowing at him. “Now I don't know who you think you talkin’ to, but I know it can't be me.”

“I just meant it’s dark outside and could be dangerous. Plus, isn't the man supposed to take out the trash?”

“Oh, so you a big man now, huh? I'll tell you what, big man,” she said, charging toward the table for her keys. “You can take out the damn trash all you want. I'm not going to stop you, cuz I won't be here.” She stormed off, slamming the front door.

He sighed with relief. That's a mess for a different day. Now what do I do with you, he thought, locking the basement door behind him.

Dialogue samples · Two-Week Dialogue Intensive

Amnesia

by Andrew McCaslin · Coursework sample

A scene from the Two-Week Dialogue Intensive, presented verbatim. A man wakes in hospital after an accident with no memory of it — or of the woman who tells him she is his wife.

A hospital scene: a man wakes after an accident remembering nothing, and talks his way through a visit from the wife he does not recognise.

Coursework sample — read in full below

“What's going on?” he asked, groggily observing his surroundings.

“You're awake,” she said, a smile lighting up her face. She stood and grabbed his hand.

“Where am I?”

“You’re in hospital.”

“What happened?” he asked, his palm pressed against his forehead as if to push the memories out.

“You’ve had an accident.”

“I don't remember an accident.” As if noticing her for the first time, he frowned. “They let you nurses wear casual clothes?“

“You’re having a laugh, right? I am your wife, darling. Don’t you recognise me?”

“No.” He attempted to shake his head, then winced in pain. “I’m sorry, I don’t. I don’t remember much. How’d the accident happen?”

“You don't remember our row? We had a bit of a disagreement about you driving in that awful snow. You stormed out, rather dramatically, and, well, I suppose you can work it out from there.”

“Okay, yeah, now I remember.” He continued quickly to avoid follow-up. “Hey, could you get the doctor for me? My head kind of hurts,” he said with a smile while squeezing her hand. “Thank you, hun.” Her body stiffened, and her eyes filled with tears. Damn, he thought. That ‘hun’ was a bad call.

“Oh, I see,” she said sadly. She pulled away and turned. “I'll get the doctor for you. And then…” she paused. “I just need a moment, I think.” Without giving him a chance to respond, she left him alone with his lie.

Published sample · Fiction

The Lazarus Code

by Andrew McCaslin

Short fiction written for the HAVOC board game community stories. Originally published at enterhavoc.com/community-stories/lazarus-code. The document below is the full story text, corrected for the spelling and grammar errors introduced when it was transferred to the website — including “ecognition” to “recognition,” “herever” to “wherever,” and “wretched” to “retched.”

Short fiction written for the HAVOC board game community stories — also listed under RPG & adventure writing.

Published sample — read in full below
Download as document (.txt) View original publication ↗

A bitter wind blew through the empty streets of Outcrag, the rundown outer slums of the Nova node proper. When the node came into being many cycles ago, the surrounding nyxlands writhed in the throes of cold. Since then, the resets had ceased, and the area was locked in a never-ending winter — a frozen purgatory.

Quora thumbed the pill-sized cylinder in her pocket, checking again to make sure it was still there. Why that creep wants this data, I don’t know. It doesn’t matter so long as it holds up its end. That’s all I need. That, and to never have to deal with Lazarus again.

Digging through her father’s past had taken months, but Lazarus’s offer was worth the effort. The damned architect and his folding bridges. May his soul rot. She wouldn’t even be in this mess if it weren’t for the architect and his nonsense scheme to connect the Core with the outer nodes.

She had never traveled to the Core, but she knew it from tales, and it scared the hell out of her. She didn’t care for the wealth and technology. Fool’s gold. Not in Nova. Not on my watch.

There was something unsettling about the Weldakin architect. His plan almost felt personal, as if he were doing it just to spite her. She didn’t trust him — not only because he represented the Core, but because something deep within her clawed for recognition or understanding. Like trying to pick up soap in a murky pond, it kept slipping through her fingers. The surprised look of recognition he gave her when they first crossed paths still chilled her.

It was enough to bring her to Outcrag, to this building. The once-proud structure now sagged under the weight of neglect, its cracked facade revealing glimpses of the rusted metal skeleton beneath.

As she crawled through the collapsed doorway, she dusted herself off and checked the valves on her thermal gear and air scrubber. Quora navigated the labyrinthine corridors of the old building, her boots crunching on broken glass and debris.

The air grew heavier with each step, the musty scent of stale air clinging to her like a second skin. Shadows danced around her in the dim light filtering through boarded-up windows, and the occasional groan of settling metal sent shivers down her spine. She passed rooms filled with overturned furniture and scattered belongings. Each step was a gamble, as the floorboards creaked and threatened to give way beneath her weight.

Finally, a set of rickety stairs descended into the darkness, leading her to the basement’s gaping maw. Why does it always have to be dingy basements? Why can’t these data harvesters have nice apartments with catering? And fresh fruit. I haven’t had fresh fruit in so long.

The air in the basement was thick with dampness. Water dripped from exposed pipes, echoing in the cavernous space. Layers of peeling paint hung like tattered shrouds from the walls, revealing corroded metal beneath. She followed her directions to a dead end. This is the entrance, right? It must be. Slow and steady, it said… It’s the only way through.

That didn’t feel right. She hit the wall with her fist to test it. It feels hard. Is it really supposed to yield? Laying her hand flat against the wall, she pressed against the surface. She pulled her hand back in shock as the wall turned smooth and liquid. Her face lit up with excitement. She had never seen anything like this. Here goes nothing. Hand outstretched, she stepped through.

Opening her eyes again, she looked across the nest, as Lazarus called it. Every surface before her was covered in putrid flesh. She had to fight not to vomit; the smell was overwhelming. This abomination of creation was an assault on the senses. Blood, decay, and other bodily fluids permeated the space, unlike anything she had ever seen.

Her eyes watered from the stench as she fought to focus her vision. Keep your shit together. Don’t give anything to this freak. Don’t give him the satisfaction. She tried to focus, but it was too much. In that moment, she was thankful not to share her adopted father’s dark vision. An eerie bioluminescent glow emanated from multiple points around the room, highlighting sickly yellows, greens, and reds. Flesh covered everything — muscle fibers stretched, convulsed, and undulated; lifeless, emotionless faces stared endlessly.

Hands, arms, and legs, like stalactites, hung from the ceiling. Blood and gore dripped and pooled onto the squelching, ever-moving collage of flesh.

Against her will, she moved forward, her steps uneasy in the unsettling atmosphere and uneven, shifting ground. The sloshing sounds underfoot made her feel as if she were trudging through a bog.

Quora cleared her throat. “Lazarus? Hello?”

She hadn’t noticed the shape that clung silently to the back wall. The figure shifted forward, and the wall stretched like something stuck to silk by static cling. The creature moved again and pulled its limbs free; she heard a dull ripping sound like the tearing of wet fabric. Yellow, viscous fluid connected the figure and the flesh wall for a moment before gravity pulled it to the ground with a plop. As it moved closer, she could see what she assumed was Lazarus. She nearly let out a shriek of surprise — a faceless form, not quite solid but not soft, rippled toward her. It glistened like thick oil.

“Ah, the Meldling,” it said. She ground her teeth at her childhood nickname, given by her father and his crew. They had found her as a baby out in the Nyx shortly after a resetstorm, cocooned in the heart of a derelict shell. They hadn’t discovered the baby until they brought the machine back and took it apart. The nickname was a reminder she never truly belonged, thrown out to the mercy of the resetstorm as she had been.

“Forgive us for losing track of time, dear. We haven’t had time to put on our face.” Lazarus turned away, and behind him, small bones rose from the floor, snapping, popping, and grinding together to form a long, thin pillar. The bones slowly doubled backward toward Quora, reaching toward the floor from where they came. The pillar stabbed downward violently before tearing loose a chunk of flesh she recognized as a human face. The bones slowly dragged the face upward — face upside down, mouth open in a silent scream. Lazarus held the face reverently and laid it upon its formless head. The flesh stitched itself together so cleanly it was as if it had always been there.

“I’ve told you before — don’t call me that.”

“Very well. So, Quora” — if its tone weren’t so dry and emotionless, she would have sworn it was mocking her — “did you bring it?”

Quora knew Lazarus was a Necrosite. Once, these beings had been like any other sentient creature, until they ventured too far into the Nyx. They came back bound by something unknowable. Necrosites didn’t walk by their own will; they were dragged back from the edges of oblivion, animated by forces ancient and strange, their bodies turned into vessels for something else. Like the dead being marched to a place of rest, they moved with a purpose not entirely their own. Whatever governed Lazarus, whatever kept his twisted form moving, remained a mystery to her.

“Yeah, I got it,” she said, pulling the metallic seed from her pocket. She knew Lazarus wouldn’t hurt her, but it knew many who could. Its reach extended into places most data harvesters couldn’t reach. It thrived on chaos, dealing in data, unsettling order wherever it could. What Lazarus wanted with a trove of religious dogma she didn’t care to ask — so long as it kept its side of the bargain.

She held the seed between her thumb and forefinger. Just as she began to approach, one of Lazarus’s limbs shot out with a sickening snap of bones. It snatched the device before she realized what had happened. The arms on the ceiling went from slowly swaying back and forth to greedily reaching for the device, passing it from one hand to the next until it made its way to Lazarus.

“It’s all there,” she said. “Now for my stuff.” The sooner I can be out of this hellhole, the better.

“So impatient,” it said, producing a similar-looking device. The unsettling assembly line of hands reversed the process, sending the seed to Quora. “And with that, our business is concluded. Use that in good conscience. Or don’t.” It bowed with a flourish before stepping back and fusing itself with the wall again.

Quora was only too glad to get the hell out of there. She used the last of her composure not to sprint out of the hive she’d already spent too much time in. Leaving the flesh cavern and entering the icy basement, she quickly rounded the corner, out of sight of the false wall, and collapsed. She shook from the experience and almost retched, her clothes still smelling of bile and viscera.

She collapsed, lying face-up on the ground. Breathing in the cool air, she began to laugh despite herself. Nothing can be worse than that, right? Comparatively, the rest of the plan is going to be smooth sailing.

Fuck the architect and fuck the bridge. They’re both going down.

Madness Unbound

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

An excerpt from the full module (11,500 words) — a story module written for ODAM Publishing for the Of Dreams and Magic RPG. The excerpt is the module’s opening: “Part One: Delve Into Madness,” the front sections (Overview, Party and Character Creation, Spoiler Warning, Setting and Atmosphere, Dreamweaver Text, and Setting the Scene), and Scene One: The DCMA, ending at the close of Stephanie Brown’s briefing. Nothing beyond that point is reproduced.

A story module for the Of Dreams and Magic RPG, written for ODAM Publishing. A difficult mid-level adventure for three to five players: the party is sent to recruit a newly awakened Anima, and finds the case far more complicated and deadly than it first appears. An excerpt — the module’s opening through Stephanie Brown’s briefing — is posted below; the full module runs to 11,500 words.

Professional sample — excerpt below

Part One: Delve Into Madness

Overview

This is a difficult mid-level module for three to five players. The players have to recruit a newly awakened Anima. They soon find out things are much more complicated and deadly than they once thought.

This story can be a stand-alone adventure or used as a sequel to another ODAM module. It is recommended characters be members of the DCMA. The estimated playtime is between four to six hours.

Party and Character Creation

This module has a good mix of combat, investigation, and social interaction. It is not necessary for the characters to be strong in all areas, but a diverse group that complements one another’s strengths and weaknesses will have an easier time finding success.

Madness Unbound is designed with the DCMA as a major plot device. It's recommended that player characters are involved, or at least on good terms with the DCMA. However, it’s possible to replace the DCMA with a different organization if that better suits your playgroup.

Spoiler Warning

If you are going to be playing Madness Unbound rather than serving as a Dreamweaver, you should stop reading here.

Setting and Atmosphere

Madness Unbound toys with the idea of sanity and what happens when it is lost or taken. The subject matter is dark and sinister, including situations and scenes of violence, torture, and mental illness. Be sure this subject matter is comfortable and appropriate for your group before proceeding.

The antagonist is a twisted sadist who tortures his victims into insanity and feeds off their anguish. Feeding off your character’s insecurities can go a long way to setting the right atmosphere for this game. Your descriptions of sounds, smells, or physical sensations the characters experience can make or break their immersion.

While this story is dark and can be graphic, remember that it is still just a game. Make sure to be mindful of your players. Being immersed in such subject matter may require periodic interruption for levity, snacks, and relief. Handle the story and its telling with care. The point is to have fun after all.

Dreamweaver Text

Any text presented in this format is information that can be read directly to the players. It often contains descriptions of locations and pertinent pieces of dialogue. While you are free to add your personal touches to the text, be sure that any points in bold are clearly delivered to the players.

Setting the Scene

If players are active agents with the DCMA their superiors have sent them to Stephanie Brown for their next assignment. She is the Director of a small satellite location and needs a group of experienced agents.

If the players are simply on good terms with the DCMA they will receive a call from Stephanie’s receptionist asking for help. He will explain that they don’t have access to many DCMA agents and they have heard good things about their group.

Scene One: The DCMA

The players arrive at a satellite location of the DCMA. They have no information other than the DCMA said it was important. They will receive further information at the briefing.

As you approach the DCMA satellite, you’re surprised to see a shoddy-looking strip mall. Pulling into the parking lot is a chore. Cracks and fissures litter the pavement like waves on an unruly ocean. Stalks of weeds have erupted between chunks of black-top.

At the far end of the building, a mini-mart sits vacant; a capsized shopping cart its only companion. On the other end, the law office of J. Dougal is a little more lively, but hardly booming with business. Nestled between them is “DCMA Cares”. A community-outreach branch of the DCMA and your destination.

Despite the condition of the exterior, the interior is rather nice. Well-groomed carpeting covers the floor, and the wallpaper is simple and homey. A young man sits at a desk at the far wall.

The receptionist welcomes you. He smiles as he gestures to the wall on his right. “Ms. Brown is waiting for you in the conference room. It’s the second door, closest to the back wall.”

You enter the conference room. There is a small, round table with just enough room for your group and Ms. Brown. On the opposite wall is an empty whiteboard. Sitting at the table under the whiteboard is Stephanie Brown.

Stephanie is a short, obese woman. She wears half-moon bifocals with a strap. When they’re not hanging around her neck, she often rests them precariously at the tip of her nose. As a result, she is often looking over her glasses at people giving her a somewhat stern expression.

There are enough seats around the table for each player. At each seat is a folder. Once players begin taking their seats, Stephanie begins.

“Thank you for coming.” She pushes her chair back as she stands, only slightly taller than when she was sitting. After groaning from the effort she opens her folder.

“My name is Stephanie Brown. I am the Community Outreach Director of this district. More appropriately I am the Anima Special Operations Director for the city limits and surrounding area.

“We had been keeping tabs on a very powerful Anima since he moved to the area. He never caused any trouble, so we never had any issue with him. He is still part of our community, so we continued to keep track of him.”

Stephanie looks over her glasses at each of you. Once she is satisfied you are all paying attention, she continues. “Sometime about a year ago, there was an incident and he had been institutionalized at Jadebrook Mental Institute before we could get to him first.

“We were in the process of having him transferred to one of our facilities when he died mysteriously. Officially, his death was labeled as a suicide, but we sent our own team to investigate. Even though we hit a lot of resistance, and couldn’t find the real cause of death for Tommy, we did find something else.

“We found another Anima, David Becker. We believe he isn’t so much crazy, as suffering from transition as a new Anima. We were able to adjust the transfer paperwork for David. Once he is in our care, we can assess his actual mental health, and help him adjust to his new life.”

End of excerpt.

Published sample · RPG & adventure writing

The Lazarus Code

by Andrew McCaslin

Short fiction written for the HAVOC board game community stories. Originally published at enterhavoc.com/community-stories/lazarus-code. The document below is the full story text, corrected for the spelling and grammar errors introduced when it was transferred to the website — including “ecognition” to “recognition,” “herever” to “wherever,” and “wretched” to “retched.”

Short fiction written for the HAVOC board game community stories.

Published sample — read in full below
Download as document (.txt) View original publication ↗

A bitter wind blew through the empty streets of Outcrag, the rundown outer slums of the Nova node proper. When the node came into being many cycles ago, the surrounding nyxlands writhed in the throes of cold. Since then, the resets had ceased, and the area was locked in a never-ending winter — a frozen purgatory.

Quora thumbed the pill-sized cylinder in her pocket, checking again to make sure it was still there. Why that creep wants this data, I don’t know. It doesn’t matter so long as it holds up its end. That’s all I need. That, and to never have to deal with Lazarus again.

Digging through her father’s past had taken months, but Lazarus’s offer was worth the effort. The damned architect and his folding bridges. May his soul rot. She wouldn’t even be in this mess if it weren’t for the architect and his nonsense scheme to connect the Core with the outer nodes.

She had never traveled to the Core, but she knew it from tales, and it scared the hell out of her. She didn’t care for the wealth and technology. Fool’s gold. Not in Nova. Not on my watch.

There was something unsettling about the Weldakin architect. His plan almost felt personal, as if he were doing it just to spite her. She didn’t trust him — not only because he represented the Core, but because something deep within her clawed for recognition or understanding. Like trying to pick up soap in a murky pond, it kept slipping through her fingers. The surprised look of recognition he gave her when they first crossed paths still chilled her.

It was enough to bring her to Outcrag, to this building. The once-proud structure now sagged under the weight of neglect, its cracked facade revealing glimpses of the rusted metal skeleton beneath.

As she crawled through the collapsed doorway, she dusted herself off and checked the valves on her thermal gear and air scrubber. Quora navigated the labyrinthine corridors of the old building, her boots crunching on broken glass and debris.

The air grew heavier with each step, the musty scent of stale air clinging to her like a second skin. Shadows danced around her in the dim light filtering through boarded-up windows, and the occasional groan of settling metal sent shivers down her spine. She passed rooms filled with overturned furniture and scattered belongings. Each step was a gamble, as the floorboards creaked and threatened to give way beneath her weight.

Finally, a set of rickety stairs descended into the darkness, leading her to the basement’s gaping maw. Why does it always have to be dingy basements? Why can’t these data harvesters have nice apartments with catering? And fresh fruit. I haven’t had fresh fruit in so long.

The air in the basement was thick with dampness. Water dripped from exposed pipes, echoing in the cavernous space. Layers of peeling paint hung like tattered shrouds from the walls, revealing corroded metal beneath. She followed her directions to a dead end. This is the entrance, right? It must be. Slow and steady, it said… It’s the only way through.

That didn’t feel right. She hit the wall with her fist to test it. It feels hard. Is it really supposed to yield? Laying her hand flat against the wall, she pressed against the surface. She pulled her hand back in shock as the wall turned smooth and liquid. Her face lit up with excitement. She had never seen anything like this. Here goes nothing. Hand outstretched, she stepped through.

Opening her eyes again, she looked across the nest, as Lazarus called it. Every surface before her was covered in putrid flesh. She had to fight not to vomit; the smell was overwhelming. This abomination of creation was an assault on the senses. Blood, decay, and other bodily fluids permeated the space, unlike anything she had ever seen.

Her eyes watered from the stench as she fought to focus her vision. Keep your shit together. Don’t give anything to this freak. Don’t give him the satisfaction. She tried to focus, but it was too much. In that moment, she was thankful not to share her adopted father’s dark vision. An eerie bioluminescent glow emanated from multiple points around the room, highlighting sickly yellows, greens, and reds. Flesh covered everything — muscle fibers stretched, convulsed, and undulated; lifeless, emotionless faces stared endlessly.

Hands, arms, and legs, like stalactites, hung from the ceiling. Blood and gore dripped and pooled onto the squelching, ever-moving collage of flesh.

Against her will, she moved forward, her steps uneasy in the unsettling atmosphere and uneven, shifting ground. The sloshing sounds underfoot made her feel as if she were trudging through a bog.

Quora cleared her throat. “Lazarus? Hello?”

She hadn’t noticed the shape that clung silently to the back wall. The figure shifted forward, and the wall stretched like something stuck to silk by static cling. The creature moved again and pulled its limbs free; she heard a dull ripping sound like the tearing of wet fabric. Yellow, viscous fluid connected the figure and the flesh wall for a moment before gravity pulled it to the ground with a plop. As it moved closer, she could see what she assumed was Lazarus. She nearly let out a shriek of surprise — a faceless form, not quite solid but not soft, rippled toward her. It glistened like thick oil.

“Ah, the Meldling,” it said. She ground her teeth at her childhood nickname, given by her father and his crew. They had found her as a baby out in the Nyx shortly after a resetstorm, cocooned in the heart of a derelict shell. They hadn’t discovered the baby until they brought the machine back and took it apart. The nickname was a reminder she never truly belonged, thrown out to the mercy of the resetstorm as she had been.

“Forgive us for losing track of time, dear. We haven’t had time to put on our face.” Lazarus turned away, and behind him, small bones rose from the floor, snapping, popping, and grinding together to form a long, thin pillar. The bones slowly doubled backward toward Quora, reaching toward the floor from where they came. The pillar stabbed downward violently before tearing loose a chunk of flesh she recognized as a human face. The bones slowly dragged the face upward — face upside down, mouth open in a silent scream. Lazarus held the face reverently and laid it upon its formless head. The flesh stitched itself together so cleanly it was as if it had always been there.

“I’ve told you before — don’t call me that.”

“Very well. So, Quora” — if its tone weren’t so dry and emotionless, she would have sworn it was mocking her — “did you bring it?”

Quora knew Lazarus was a Necrosite. Once, these beings had been like any other sentient creature, until they ventured too far into the Nyx. They came back bound by something unknowable. Necrosites didn’t walk by their own will; they were dragged back from the edges of oblivion, animated by forces ancient and strange, their bodies turned into vessels for something else. Like the dead being marched to a place of rest, they moved with a purpose not entirely their own. Whatever governed Lazarus, whatever kept his twisted form moving, remained a mystery to her.

“Yeah, I got it,” she said, pulling the metallic seed from her pocket. She knew Lazarus wouldn’t hurt her, but it knew many who could. Its reach extended into places most data harvesters couldn’t reach. It thrived on chaos, dealing in data, unsettling order wherever it could. What Lazarus wanted with a trove of religious dogma she didn’t care to ask — so long as it kept its side of the bargain.

She held the seed between her thumb and forefinger. Just as she began to approach, one of Lazarus’s limbs shot out with a sickening snap of bones. It snatched the device before she realized what had happened. The arms on the ceiling went from slowly swaying back and forth to greedily reaching for the device, passing it from one hand to the next until it made its way to Lazarus.

“It’s all there,” she said. “Now for my stuff.” The sooner I can be out of this hellhole, the better.

“So impatient,” it said, producing a similar-looking device. The unsettling assembly line of hands reversed the process, sending the seed to Quora. “And with that, our business is concluded. Use that in good conscience. Or don’t.” It bowed with a flourish before stepping back and fusing itself with the wall again.

Quora was only too glad to get the hell out of there. She used the last of her composure not to sprint out of the hive she’d already spent too much time in. Leaving the flesh cavern and entering the icy basement, she quickly rounded the corner, out of sight of the false wall, and collapsed. She shook from the experience and almost retched, her clothes still smelling of bile and viscera.

She collapsed, lying face-up on the ground. Breathing in the cool air, she began to laugh despite herself. Nothing can be worse than that, right? Comparatively, the rest of the plan is going to be smooth sailing.

Fuck the architect and fuck the bridge. They’re both going down.

The Shared Dream · RPG & adventure writing

Reflection Epilogues

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

Three selected epilogues from a larger set of sixteen written for The Shared Dream board game. Each card is drawn on a stated condition and read aloud in second person as the ending of that game. The three kept here show the range of the set: a Golden Age comic-book villain’s rant in “Foiled Again!”, slapstick rather than horror from the killer-clown deck in “What, No Anvil?”, and a quiet, hopeful ending in “A New Day.”

EXPLOSIVE NIGHTLIFE

Foiled Again!

Draw this card if the players are victorious and no bombs went off.

“How?! How could you have disarmed all my bombs? Those were specially crafted by yours truly. Not just any Tom, Dick, or Harry could’a disarmed one, let alone all of ‘em!”

Bryce the Damned lay bound at your feet rambling about his fool-proof plan and how it’s inconceivable that he could have been thwarted “by the likes of you.” You hope that this will be the last time you see this fool, but you realize it probably won’t be.

“You haven’t seen the last of me! No mere jail cell can hold me! I’ll be back, just you wait. And when I get free again, you do-gooders will pay! Oh, yes, you’ll all pay dearly!”

DEAD SERIOUS

What, No Anvil?

Draw this card if the players are victorious.

The clown stands before you. He looks just like an ordinary clown. Nothing special or sinister. He places his fists on his hips with a huff and begins stamping toward you in an exaggerated way as if for comedic effect.

He pulls out a knife and stabs you, but the knife bends. He tries again and it bends again. He looks at it, scratching his head, and stabs himself. The blade goes clean through his stomach and he lets out a yelp. A comically large frown appears on his face.

He pulls out a gun and pulls the trigger. “BANG!” A small flag pops out of the barrel with the word “BANG!” written on it. Frustrated, he pulls the flag out and tries it again. The same thing happens except the flag is green instead of red. He shakes the gun and points it at his face. The gun goes off with a loud explosion. When the dust settles, the gun barrel has been peeled back like a banana peel, and the clown’s face is covered in gunpowder. With one last gunpowder filled puff of air, the clown falls backward sending up a cloud of smoke. He’s no threat to anyone anymore.

BEAST AT THE DOOR

A New Day

Draw this card if the Beast has been defeated.

As the Beast dies a cool breeze blows. It’s a welcome change to the heat of battle. You close your eyes and allow it to wash over you, cooling the sweat as it drips down your body. The air smells fresh and you begin to hear birds chirping in the distance.

You open your eyes to see the sun peeking over the horizon. The warm, gentle rays of light blanket the city as if protecting it. You smile as you’re enveloped in a comforting cocoon of light from the sun.

The Beast is dead and life goes on. Most of the city is unaware of what really happened, but its reign of terror is over. Today is a new day.

The Shared Dream · RPG & adventure writing

Human Sacrifice — Reflection Deck

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

One complete investigation chain from the Human Sacrifice reflection deck for The Shared Dream: the deck’s opening dream, then Sandy Baker’s chain in full — her Start, Cards 1–5, the Old House: Bedroom conclusion, and the rules card that governs how Sandy moves with the investigator. A chain of location cards with read-aloud text, tests, and consequences, following a survivor of the ritual at the Phantom House twenty years on.

Intro

A thick fog envelopes an old, abandoned mansion. Symbols are crudely scratched on every surface of what was once the living room. Lit candles line the room casting eerie shadows. It's hard to tell if the flickering flames are creating the illusion of a macabre masquerade, or if the shadows are truly alive. Five hooded figures stand in a circle, each at a point of the pentagram carved into the floor. They all hold hands as they chant incoherently. A black mist coalesces in a maelstrom at the center of the group. The chanting continues as the room is thrown into chaos. The candles are snuffed out in an instant leaving the moon to fill the room with a faint, blue glow. Anything not nailed down is furiously thrown across the room, occasionally hitting one of the five in the center of the room. The room stills and even the mist stops swirling, remaining frozen in place. A moment passes of silence and stillness. As the moments stretch on, the circle is broken as one of the figures begins to reach toward the mist. “No!” Another screams as it grabs the outstretched hand. The mist quickly collapses into a singular point, then stretches into a thin point and opens, exposing nothing but inky blackness. The silence is shattered with a low growl emanating from the portal. Two red eyes begin to emerge as smoky fingers grasp either side of the portal. The figures stand still in fear as a grotesque head slowly emerges. “Run,” the familiar voice commands as it lowers its hood revealing a male in his late teens/early twenties. He leaps through the opening, driving the figure back and closing the portal. As the room goes still you see the lifeless body of the brave man who seemingly saved the others. The other four run from the house as the body catches fire and quickly engulfs the room. You wake in a cold sweat hoping that it was just a dream, knowing full well there is no such thing.

Sandy Baker: Reunion Start

Your investigation begins at the Old House Exterior. The dream didn’t give you much to go on, but it did give you a house. Since the house has reappeared, it seems like the most logical place to start. As you approach the house from your dreams you notice a woman standing outside looking up at it. She notices you as you approach. “Nothing has changed. It’s exactly as I remember it.” She turns to you, then back to the house. “You’re one of them, aren’t you?” She nods to herself. “I’m not an Anima anymore, but I can tell that much at least. I tried getting in, but I can’t for some reason. I think I know how to fix that.” She begins to walk away before turning one more time. “You coming?”

Take the Sandy Baker card from the deck Your investigation continues at The School...

Card 1 The School

Arriving at the school Sandy reverts to the position she was in when you first met her: staring silently. Eventually she speaks. “This is where we all met. Shocking, I know. Bunch’a kids meeting in a school.” She smiles, but it quickly fades. “I love this place. Not because I love learning, or had such great friends, or any other after school special BS like that. But it’s where I met him...Johnny.” Her smile reappears. “He really was the best of us. Smart, strong, handsome...brave. We never knew why he wanted to hang with a bunch of losers like us. Billy was just some punk kid being shipped from home to home for as long as people were willing to put up with him. Carlos was just your typical nerd who got picked on and beat up every day. I was a trainwreck, and Jodi?” She spits in disgust. “Let’s just say I’m glad she’s dead. “I’m done here. Let’s go.” Your investigation continues at The Park…

Card 2 The Park

“This was my favorite place of ours. We’d come here when we could get away from the others and just walk, or have a picnic, or just lay on the grass and watch the clouds. We’d talk about the future. Our future. “We could just get away. No a-holes from school, or teachers breathing down our necks. No crappy home lives. It was just us. We could pretend, if just for a moment, we were like any other kids. “It was here that he had the idea that we could be like any other kids. In fact, the day of the ritual he brought me here, gave me this,” she thumbs a small ring on the ring-finger of her right hand. “And promised me that after the ritual, nothing could stop us from being together. We were going to run away together and nothing, not parents, not school, and not even our dreams could stop us. “There’s one more place I have to go before we get this taken care of.”

Your investigation continues at the Warehouse...

Card 3 Warehouse

“This is where we’d come to hang out. We’d all just kinda sit around and smoke, break things, set fires. Ya know, dumb kid stuff. That is until we ‘woke up.’ “We all thought we were superheroes after that. Carlos actually was. Tights and everything. But then things got too real. We didn’t know what we were doing. We used our magic recklessly and ended up summoning Jodi’s Nemesis. Thing made her sick as a dog. She could barely stand, let alone fight it. It almost killed us all. After that we wanted out. “We met up here that day to regroup and go over the details of the ritual for the millionth time. We were all so excited… “Would you mind taking me to the DCMA? If anyone can help us, they’ll be there. I’ll explain everything to you there. And I wouldn’t mind seeing it again.” Your investigation continues at the DCMA HQ...

Card 4 DCMA HQ

“He’s alive! I’ve been seeing him in my dreams. He needs my help. I kept seeing those places we went in my dreams, so I think I had to retrace my steps that day before I could go back. I also saw this,” she takes off the ring she showed you earlier. “We each needed an item, the thing that meant most to us. I think this is my ticket back inside, but I don’t know how or why.” As she explains everything you see an almost crazed look in her eyes. She’s clearly being manipulated by a reaver, or worse. From the description of the ritual, and what you saw in your dream, you know you need to cleanse and destroy the item. This will need some convincing.

You can either choose to convince her to hand over the object, or take it by force. If you try to convince her, make a Social test. Otherwise, your investigation continues at the Old House…

Make a Social test: <2: She is horrified at the suggestion and runs off. You think you know where she’s headed. YRCA Old House Exterior 1 3+: “I guess this whole thing is better than just me and him, now. Make sure you give it back when you’re done” YRCA Old House Exterior 2

Make a Magic test: <0: Add a taint to this location. This is in addition to any other source of taint. 0-2: Nothing happens. 3+: The curse is broken and the item is destroyed.

Your investigation is complete.

Card 5 Old House Exterior

Arriving back at the old house, you see Sandy trying frantically to get in. She screams as you approach. “I want to go back in! I hate it out here! There’s nothing here for me!” Although you hear nothing, Sandy appears to ‘listen’ to the house, speaking to her. She turns to you and pulls a small knife. Her wailing face shifts into an other-worldly grimace.

“Finally! Finally it’ll let me back in! And all it’ll take is getting rid of you!”

Sandy lunges at you with the knife.

Make a Combat test: <2: You take one damage as she fights back, but you are able to wrestle the ring from her grasp. 3+: You incapacitate her and take the ring. Gain 5 Nightmare.

Either way, your reflection continues in the Old House: Bedroom.

Old House: Bedroom

As if it wasn’t malevolent enough, the house seems to HATE that you have the ring in your possession. The walls shake, the low groans growing into outright screams of pain and anger. You can tell the ring has some amount of power over this place. You must spend 6 Conviction to activate the ring and cleanse the room. This Conviction can be spent over multiple actions and over multiple day phases. Any other player in the Bedroom can also spend Conviction towards this task.

Once the 6 conviction is spent, the bedroom goes entirely silent. Suddenly, you are outside the house.

Remove the Old House: Bedroom from the game, along with any enemies or taint on it. Your personal reflection is complete.

Sandy Baker: Rules Place a white cube on the Old House to represent Sandy. Every day phase after this one Sandy moves toward your next reflection destination at a movement of two, and she always takes the shortest path. She only moves after your turn. You may take her with you as an action (so moving with Sandy would cost one action for the movement, and one for taking her with for a total of two actions). If you take her with you, she will not move on her own for that day phase. If you are with her she leaves one taint behind at each location crossed through. If you are not with her she leaves two taint behind, instead. If she is on a location at the beginning of the day phase add the required number of taint. She stops and waits for you at your next destination, accumulating taint as normal. When your investigation is complete, remove this card, and the cube from the game.

The Shared Dream · RPG & adventure writing

Late Arrival — Reflection Deck: “Portal to Hell”

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

One complete storyline from the Late Arrival reflection deck for The Shared Dream, presented in full: the deck’s introduction plus the whole “Portal to Hell” chain — Start (The Hospital) and Cards 1–5 (DCMA HQ, Library, Melisandra’s Alley, Old House 1, Old House 2). The deck’s other storylines — “Home is Where the Heart is,” “The Void,” and “Exorcism” — circle the same Phantom House and are not reproduced here.

Intro

The Phantom House looms dauntingly over you. A black shroud envelopes it. Flash. The house is gone. An empty field remains with no sign of ever having anything on it. Flash. The house is back as if it had never left. The door opens and you float inside as if on a conveyor belt. Voices can be heard within. Their chanting sounds normal enough, as normal as chanting can sound. As you are drawn closer the sounds begin to get hauntingly distorted. The sounds slow to a crawl, then speed up to an unnatural pace as if to catch up with the time they've lost. The sounds distort as if played on a warped record. You see a circle of five hooded figures surrounded by candles and symbols. As their chanting intensifies, the scene begins to fade as if watching it on an old VHS tape. The looping screech in their voices is almost deafening until it stops abruptly. Everything returns to as it was. In fact, time seems to freeze. The figures are still, the chanting has stopped, even the candle flames are eerily locked in place. Flash. The scene changes. A pillar of swirling black smoke stands in the middle of the five figures. Debris hangs suspended in air. Flash. One figure stands, arm outstretched toward the pillar, another has their hand grasping the wrist of the first. Flash. A portal has replaced the smoke and one of the figures is mid-leap and halfway in the portal. Flash. You stand alone in the room. Nothing remains except the portal. Inky blackness emerges from it, covering the room. A humanoid figure spills from the portal covered in oily sludge. This grotesque mockery of birth makes your stomach turn. The figure begins pushing itself up, its movements are frantic and twitchy. The thing moves like a glitching video. Frame by frame it seems to jump into different positions without moving. As it opens its mouth to scream static fills all your senses for what feels like an eternity. In the days that follow, disturbed as you are by the dream, it is the last one you have. Something is very, VERY wrong.

Portal to Hell Start

Your investigation begins at The Hospital Ever since that crazy dream, your sleep has been dreamless. In fact, it appears everyone has been without their dreams. People have been acting crazy, violent, or just plain careless. Most people walk around as if they haven't slept in weeks. “I don't know what's going on,” Asha says. “I've been working here for a long time and I have never seen anything like it. Without their dreams people been acting out their issues 'stead of working through 'em in their sleep. “Place to go would probably be the DCMA. If anyone knows what's goin' on, it'd be them, I'm sure.”

Your investigation continues at the DCMA HQ...

Card 1 DCMA HQ

“We've all had the same dream,” the DCMA employee says. “That is, all us Anima did. It's something to do with that house, I'm sure. We've purified it. I mean, I thought we did, and here we are getting another creepy dream about the house. Then nothing, no more dreams, and magic seems to be acting strangely. You can't tell me you don't think that's weird. “I’ve been looking into it for a bit now; something just never sat right for me about that place. From everything I’ve seen, it looks like there may be a bridge, or something connecting the waking world with...somewhere else. I suspect that’s what’s keeping it here. If we sever the connection, we can hopefully destroy the house once and for all. “I'm afraid that whatever that thing was at the end of the dream is still somehow bound to the house. You can probably find some more info about the house over at the library, I'll look into a few things on my end as well.”

Your investigation continues at the Library...

Card 2 Library

You spend a good deal of time researching this house. Most of what you find is about the ritual that happened twenty years ago. Five teens broke into the abandoned house and did a “satanic” ritual which caused the death of one, Johnny Campbell, and burned the house down. You eventually find the original owner, Oliver Harris. Though he passed away almost a century ago, you recognize the name. He was suspected to be both a powerful magician and a very sick man. In his early life he was a snake oil salesman, but once he was suspected to have become a magician, he turned to dark arts. He had claimed his home was a portal to hell itself and that's where he got his vast power. Eventually, the neighborhood, out of fear and self-preservation, hanged him on the tree in the backyard. They buried him in a shallow grave by the tree and tried burning his house down. Witnesses claim the house burned for hours, but the house was never consumed. There's only one person you can think of who can help you now.

Your investigation continues at Melisandra’s Alley...

Card 3 Melisandra’s Alley

“I remember that.” Melisandra says sadly when you ask her about Oliver. “The poor soul needed some guidance, and maybe this would have never happened.” She shakes her head. “It wasn't for me to interfere, but I remember it like it was yesterday. “There is a lot of evil surrounding that house. I'm afraid things are a bit more complicated than just cleansing the place. You'll have to destroy the connection Oliver made with the other realm. “That will get you one step closer to destroying the house, but you still have the Void to worry about.” You remember learning about voids. They are a literal void of magic. Anima who have gone against them have had a real hard time of it, if they've even survived at all. It all makes sense now. “I fear the void is bound to the house as well and to defeat it, you must sever the connection and destroy the house.” Melisandra gives you a few supplies giving you a +1 to Magic for the ritual.

If you are playing with Sandy's deck, draw a card now. Once that card is resolved, continue as normal.

Your investigation continues at the Old House 1…

Card 4 Old House 1

You begin setting up for the ritual. Despite the importance and urgency, you know you need to take your time. There are a lot of complex elements, and one misstep can have terrible consequences. You check your notes for the third time trying to get the exact configuration and layout of the candles, salt, and other assortment of ingredients. As you look up you notice a figure appearing before you. At first it looks like a shadowy humanoid, but as time goes on you see the figure of a man becoming clearer as if a thick fog is dissipating. The features solidify showing a middle-aged man with a thin moustache and dark, shifty eyes. He is well groomed, good looking, and by his stance and composure, he’s well aware of it. He is dressed as you would expect to see from a noble gentleman in the late 19th century. “I am Oliver Harris, and you are trespassing!”

Your investigation continues at the Old House 2…

Card 5 Old House 2

The spirit identifying itself as Oliver Harris approaches you. You notice his coloring is off as if someone adjusted the colors on a TV set. The fabric of his clothes looks dull, but clean. His skin looks overly pale, and even his hair looks like someone covered the inky blackness with a fine grey mist. Though he looks solid, you imagine if you tried to touch him your hand would pass right through “You have come here to destroy me, I know it. Though your motives may be different, the result will be the same.” He looks at the house for a moment, then back at you. “I am bound to this place as long as it is bound here. Once the house is destroyed, well, let’s say that things in the place on the other end of that portal will come looking for me. I can’t have that.”

Make a Magic test <2: You take 1 damage 3+: You destroy the spirit and can now focus on the ritual at hand.

Your investigation is complete

The Shared Dream · RPG & adventure writing

Johnny Cards — Fractured Magic

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

The six-card Fractured Magic deck for The Shared Dream, with its rules, presented in full. One card is turned over each night phase; once all six are out, Johnny enters the field at the Phantom House — and he cannot truly be defeated until every player has completed their personal reflections. Every curse can be lifted the same way: a player voluntarily accepts a point of Doubt to remove it.

There are six Fractured Magic cards. During each night phase players must turn over one card and follow its directions. Once all cards are turned over Johnny enters the field in the next night phase and can act immediately. He always appears at the Phantom House. Players have six turns to complete their personal reflections. Doing so will force Johnny to emerge once all players have finished their reflections. Players cannot defeat Johnny until everyone has completed their reflections and have read their conclusion. They may then fight him as normal. Defeating Johnny before that will instead cause him to respawn at the house’s location at full power.

Something's Wrong

-1 to Magic scores for all players. This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

Sleeper Again

All Magic scores are set to zero. However, any artifact or special card affecting the score with a bonus or drawback still apply (This card and the Something's Wrong card adjust Magic to -1). This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

This is a Nightmare

All players add one nightmare to their nightmare track. This can never be removed. Players will always have at least one nightmare. This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

Just a Daydream

All Animus immediately reverts back to their Anima state at the beginning of each night phase. This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

You're Not as Great as You Think You Are

Your max conviction is reduced by 1. This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

Magic is Just a Distant Dream

All conviction costs are increased by 1. This card remains in effect until the end of the game.

By voluntarily accepting a point of Doubt, a player may (ignore the effects of this card for the rest of the game) remove this card and its effects from the game.

The Shared Dream · RPG & adventure writing

House Movement and Rules

by Andrew McCaslin · Written for ODAM Publishing

Excerpt — one complete scenario chart. Rules writing for The Shared Dream: how the Phantom House moves and triggers in the Human Sacrifice scenario, rolled fresh at the start of every night phase.

The Phantom House is a unique factor in The Shared Dream and works differently depending on the scenario being played. Every day a d6 is rolled to determine the house's effect for that day.

Scenario 1: Human Sacrifice

At the beginning of each night phase, before doing anything else, trigger the house. Roll a d6 and follow the chart below based on the outcome:

6 – No movement. Place one taint on this tile. If that is not possible, place it on the nearest location tile. If two locations are the same distance, place one on the location with the most taint. Any player who lands on this space, or is already on this space gains one Nightmare, and lose one Conviction. This effect lasts until the next time the house is triggered.

5 – Roll a d6 and move that many spaces North. If the house goes off the board continue the count at the Southernmost tile in the same column.

4 - Roll a d6 and move that many spaces West. If the house goes off the board continue the count at the Easternmost tile in the same row.

3 - Roll a d6 and move that many spaces East. If the house goes off the board continue the count at the Westernmost tile in the same row.

2 - Roll a d6 and move that many spaces South. If the house goes off the board continue the count at the Northernmost tile in the same column.

1 – Nothing happens.

Hero: Reborn — game concept package

by Andrew McCaslin · Coursework sample

A complete original game package, presented verbatim: the concept document for the open-world action RPG “Hero: Reborn” — gods living among us, holding down regular 9-to-5 jobs and fighting crime at night — with the two character bios (Mr. Wonder and Sovereign) that support it, built on the same template of biography, two truths, and one lie the character tells himself. The one correction applied is a typo in the Sovereign bio: “ponds” read as “pawns.”

A complete original game package: the concept document (gods holding down regular 9-to-5 jobs, fighting crime at night; a hero whose aggressive play literally makes him weaker), plus the Mr. Wonder and Sovereign character bios built on the same template — biography, two truths, one lie the character tells himself.

Coursework sample — read in full below

What if gods walked among us? What if they were your friends, your family, your neighbors? What if they held down regular 9-to-5 jobs, but at night they wore capes and fought crime?

What if one of these gods lost his way?

After a tragedy befalls Ethan Miller, he becomes determined to stop villains at all costs. As his alter ego, Mr. Wonder, he grows colder and more brutal in mindset and action. He believes that any collateral damage – even death and injury – is a necessary sacrifice to prevent villains from causing even greater harm.

As his morals continue to decline, some members of The Wonder League decide to intervene. They explain that he has lost his way and forgotten what it truly means to be a hero. Using irreversible magic, they bind his powers, informing him that he will only regain them when he relearns what it means to be a hero.

In Hero: Reborn, players experience the weight of having godly powers and the consequences that come with them. Do you allow a villain to escape in order to disarm a bomb, or do you chase after the villain to put them down for good and let the bomb wreak havoc?

Player choices will determine not only the path they take but also the ultimate strength of the hero they become. A selfish, aggressive play style may be fun and rewarding in the short term, but it will ultimately lead to a weaker overall character.

Hero: Reborn challenges players to confront the complexities of heroism, where every choice carries weight and shapes the kind of hero they ultimately become.

During a fierce battle with a supervillain, Mr. Wonder found himself facing a terrible dilemma. The fight caused significant collateral damage, and a falling statue nearly crushed a child. Mr. Wonder instinctively raced to save the child, succeeding just in time. However, his heroic act allowed the villain to escape. In a cruel twist of fate, the fleeing villain destroyed part of a nearby building, and Camille Miller, Ethan's wife, was caught in the destruction. She was killed instantly.

This devastating event shattered Mr. Wonder. The weight of his actions and powers became almost unbearable. He grappled with guilt and regret, agonizing over his choices. He became convinced that if he hadn't stopped to save the child, Camille and the other victims would still be alive.

Haunted by grief and consumed by a desperate need to prevent further tragedies, Mr. Wonder embraced a chilling new philosophy. He became colder, more ruthless, and utterly determined to eliminate villains at any cost. Collateral damage, even the loss of innocent lives, became a secondary concern in his relentless pursuit of justice.

The game begins with the player taking control of Mr. Wonder at the peak of his power. He soars towards a supervillain's base, fueled by vengeance and a disregard for collateral damage. Players are given free rein to unleash devastating attacks upon the base and its occupants. After a brief but intense boss battle, a cutscene unfolds. The Crusader, a fellow superhero, arrives in his sleek jet, and after a sarcastic barb from Mr. Wonder, the Crusader swiftly subdues him with a potent gas, rendering him unconscious. The scene fades to black, and the following cutscene then ensues.

Act 1: Seeds of Doubt

The Setup: Mr. Wonder, once a celebrated hero, has become jaded and ruthless after a personal tragedy. He now prioritizes stopping villains at all costs, even if it means collateral damage. Meanwhile, a new threat emerges: Sovereign, a being from a destroyed universe, is manipulating Omega shards – fragments of his former reality – to grant humans superpowers and bend them to his will.

Mission Examples:

Investigate the Nexus Uprising: The first mission throws players into chaos as they confront mind-controlled humans with strange new abilities. They must uncover the source of this phenomenon and the connection to the stolen Omega shards.

Rescue the Oracle: A brilliant scientist has discovered Sovereign's plan but is captured. Players must infiltrate a heavily guarded facility to rescue her and gain vital information.

Betrayal: A member of the Wonder League and a friend of Ethan’s is found to have been under Sovereign’s sway unbeknownst to him. Ethan must fight his friend to help him, but will he treat him like any other villain, or does Ethan hold back for fear of irrevocably harming his friend? This becomes the first major test for Ethan and the player.

Act 2: The Nexus Unveiled

Escalation: Sovereign reveals his true intentions: to terraform Earth and absorb the life essence of all beings, using the Nexus points as his instruments. He manipulates public opinion, promising a utopian future while secretly twisting the very fabric of reality. Mr. Wonder must expose Sovereign's deception and sabotage the Nexus points, but doing so risks alienating the public he swore to protect.

Mission Examples:

The Price of Peace: Sovereign activates a Nexus point in a densely populated city. Players must race against time to disable it, choosing between a quick but destructive method or a riskier approach with less collateral damage.

The People's Champion: Sovereign stages a public demonstration of his power, "healing" the sick and promising an end to suffering. Players must expose his lies and reveal the mind control behind his "miracles," but doing so could turn the public against them.

Moral Crossroads: A mission where players must choose between stopping a rampaging Nexus being and saving innocent lives, forcing them to confront the grey areas of heroism.

Act 3: Unity and Sacrifice

The Endgame: Sovereign initiates the Unity Cycle, a process that will weaken him but also accelerate his plan. Mr. Wonder must rally allies, infiltrate Sovereign's stronghold, and disrupt the Unity Cycle before it's too late. The final confrontation will test his resolve and force him to choose the kind of hero he wants to be.

Mission Examples:

Unlikely Alliances: Mr. Wonder must convince former enemies and skeptical heroes to join his cause, even if it means compromising his own morals.

The Heart of the Nexus: A desperate assault on Sovereign's heavily fortified headquarters, where players must navigate treacherous traps and face off against his most powerful creations.

Breaking the Cycle: The climax of the game, where players must disrupt the Unity Cycle while battling a weakened but still formidable Sovereign. Choices made during this fight will determine the ending and the fate of the world.

This open-world action RPG starts with a tutorial, after which players can fly through the city to their first main mission. Initially, the city is relatively empty of activities. However, after completing this mission, the city comes alive with events: races against speedsters, timed challenges, random crimes (thugs snatching purses, villain shootouts), and side missions that flesh out the world and offer opportunities for character growth.

Mr. Wonder begins with reduced power. Completing challenges, tasks, and missions earns him experience to level up. However, collateral damage reduces experience earned, with a minimum of 10% awarded. For example, a 1,000-experience mission guarantees at least 100. After each mission, a briefing details experience gains and penalties: civilian injuries (-50 points each), deaths (-250), and structural damage (-1 point per $1,000).

A "hold back" toggle mitigates collateral damage. It prevents attacks on civilians and reduces structural damage. An accessibility option disables all collateral damage, allowing players to focus on the story and action without penalty.

These options give players full autonomy over their playstyle and character development.

Every 1,000 experience points earned grants one hero point, which players can allocate to four stats: Health (damage absorption and regeneration), Energy (speed and stamina), Resilience (strength and damage resistance), and Other (powers like heat vision and combo techniques).

Each stat also unlocks a skill tree with abilities and techniques tied to its level. For example, "Supersonic Speed" might require a level 25 Energy stat and the "Super Speed" perk. Stats are upgraded with hero points, while skill tree techniques are purchased with experience points.

Combat stances are key to gameplay and character builds. There are three: Quick, Power, and a fully customized option. Each stance has unique purchasable techniques. Power moves are exclusive to the Power stance, and quick moves to the Quick stance.

Quick Stance: Excels at mobility and swiftly defeating weaker foes. Players zip through combat, hitting multiple enemies. Blocking triggers super-speed evasion, dodging bullets and punches. However, evading drains the Energy-linked stamina meter. The ultimate move slows time for everyone but Mr. Wonder, allowing rapid enemy takedowns.

Power Stance: Specializes in high damage and crowd control. Movement is slightly reduced but still enhanced by super speed. Blocking adopts a classic superhero pose (fists on hips), deflecting attacks while draining the Resilience meter. The ultimate move grants temporary invulnerability and immunity to knockdowns and knockbacks.

Custom Stance: Offers full customization. Players can choose light and heavy attacks, special moves, block animations, and even the ultimate move from either the Quick or Power stance, creating a truly personalized combat style.

In the final Sovereign confrontation, players face the activated, non-deactivatable Unity core. They choose: destroy it, causing a massive cataclysm but ending Sovereign, or sacrifice themselves to absorb the energy, nullifying it and defeating Sovereign at the cost of their life.

This choice is independent of hero points. Destroying the machine triggers a devastating explosion, permanently crippling the city and causing widespread, long-term environmental damage.

Choosing sacrifice grants a large mid-cutscene experience boost. If the player's total experience is below a threshold, Mr. Wonder dies, unable to withstand the energy. The facility is destroyed, but collateral damage is minimal. News reports confirm his death.

If the experience boost meets the threshold, Mr. Wonder survives. Initially, his fate is ambiguous. However, Mr. Wonder dramatically walks through the smoky rubble as the music swells. He has learned what it is to put others before himself and now is the man that he once was physically, mentally, and emotionally. He is a hero.

Character bio — Mr. Wonder

Character name: Ethan Miller AKA, Mr. Wonder

Age: 33

Place of origin: Alternate Universe but arrived in Western New York, USA

Family members and Friends

Camille Miller: wife (deceased)

Numerous friends within the Guild of Heroes. Chief among them, Sentinel and the Crusader.

Brief biography

Mr. Wonder originated from a universe that is non-material. After a cataclysm shifted their universe into another, it destroyed both sending their denizens into our universe. As a non-material entity, Mr. Wonder had to find a consciousness to merge with in order to become material.

He found humanity and was able to manifest himself as Mr. Wonder. Though there were plenty of other heroes around, he quickly became known as righteous, steadfast, and was recognized as the most powerful.

During one fateful battle, Mr. Wonder stopped to save a civilian allowing the enemy to escape. Mr. Wonder found out later that during the villain's escape he destroyed part of a building where Camille was, killing her.

Two truths about the character

He is the most powerful hero on the planet, if not beyond. Such a power weighs heavily on him, though different now than in the past. He feels the consequences of the lives lost as a result of his actions.

He always strives to do what is right. However, after losing his wife, his concept of what is right has been notably changed.

One lie the character tells about themself

He must stop his villains at all costs. What collateral damage may ensue by such actions pales in comparison to what these villains would do unchecked. It is a necessary evil. If 10,000 people must die so a million can live, those are acceptable odds.

Appearance details

He is a handsome man in his early thirties. He has a powerful build, but still moves with grace. He has brown hair and blue eyes. He has a blue suit with red accents and a red cape. There is a star in the middle of his chest that seems to glow with golden light.

Enemies

Every good superhero needs to have a rogues’ gallery, and Mr. Wonder is no exception. However, his main villain, his arch enemy if you will, is Sovereign. Sovereign is an entity that followed him from his original universe.

Where Mr. Wonder found Humanity to merge with, Sovereign found technology. Mr. Wonder has not knowingly seen his mortal enemy since they arrived in this universe, but he's been there, watching, waiting, ready to enact his diabolical schemes when the time is right.

Character bio — Sovereign

Character name: Sovereign

Age: unknown

Place of origin: originally from the same universe as Mr. Wonder.

Family members and Friends

No family or friends. He uses people like objects or pawns in his game. He sees them as little more than Stepping Stones to get where he needs to go.

Brief biography

In his original universe, there was a clash between him and the being that is now Mr. Wonder. The clash was so mighty and significant it shifted the trajectory of their Universe causing it to collide with another. The entities therein were thrown throughout the greater cosmos. Many of them, including Mr. Wonder and Sovereign were thrown into our reality.

Since Sovereign came from a non-material universe, he was unable to survive for long in our universe. He needed to find a sentient species to meld his consciousness with and form materially. He found technology. Sentient AI became his vessel through which he could interact with material reality. He developed complete control of technology. It gave him a boon to allow him to inhabit technology directly, or be a part of an unseen web of technological energy.

After trial and error he determined it is best to assimilate a population by infiltrating and laying the proverbial infrastructure before taking over.

Two truths about the character

He is extremely intelligent. He has no room for love or compassion and like the machinery he inhabits he is very cold and calculating, though not without the capacity for emotional outbursts.

He wants everyone and everything to be unified as one being. He hates material reality and looks to ultimately terraform this universe into a new version of his former universe by consuming the essence of living things and destroying all matter. He has done this on many worlds prior and now has his eyes set on Earth.

One lie the character tells about themself

Physical reality is a curse and only through Unity can we rise above and break from its chains. There is no one better to enact such a plan than he.

Appearance details

Sovereign can take command of any technology. His true form is unseen, but he mostly chooses to manifest through highly advanced nanobots that resemble the physical makeup of a species he is infiltrating or otherwise attempting to mimic. It will look identical to a normal being of that species, down to the biomechanics and even production of blood and other natural fluids and phenomena. The form he has chosen to take as a human is of a man, early forties, with short dark hair and an average build. Fairly unremarkable to look at. He takes a more menacing facade when appearing as his true self. So when he doesn't need his disguise, he tends to appear as a black or smoky gray humanoid entity wearing body armor.

Enemies

Mr. Wonder is the only person he views as an actual threat. He still remembers their battle that led them to where they are, and assumed he would have a similar level of power in this realm. After careful study and analysis, he determined that the power he wields is in fact proportional and therefore is treated with caution. His work on Earth must be more subtle to avoid direct confrontation with Mr Wonder as Sovereign is in a weakened state just before his Unity cycle.

About

About me

I’m a writer based in Columbus, Ohio. I work for clients — ghostwriting books, building narrative for games and graphic novels, and writing for tabletop RPGs and board games.

I got my start the direct way: answering a publisher’s forum call for writers. That led to a first paid RPG scenario for ODAM Publishing in Columbus in 2017, a place on the publisher’s short list for later releases, and then a staff role as Director of Operations from 2018 to 2021.

Today I work freelance. The through-line in all of it is the same: take someone’s story, world, or game seriously, agree the shape of it up front, and then write it carefully, in the voice the project needs — not my own.
